newsitem.title: USA: MCI Chairman knocks down Baby Bell merger.
newsitem.headline: MCI Chairman knocks down Baby Bell merger.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp. Chairman Bert Roberts Thursday said if AT&T Corp. merged with a Baby Bell company, there was only a "remote" chance that MCI would do the same.

Speaking at the same forum where AT&T Chairman Robert Allen opened the door to such a union, Roberts said he would be "fundamentally opposed" if AT&T went ahead and proposed a merger with a Baby Bell.
"I think it will be, I would have to say, a very remote and a very complex set of circumstances before we would consider," merging with a Baby Bell, he said.

The MCI chairman said an AT&T merger with a Baby Bell would spur the other local telephone operating companies to rethink their strategies. Speaking at a Boston College's Chief Executives Club luncheon, Roberts was joined by Alan Rudge, deputy chief executive of British Telecommunications Plc, MCI's proposed merger partner.

"If it happens, and the regulators would approve it, Alan (Rudge) and I will be standing at MCI headquarters doors and taking a list of names from (Baby Bells) who obviously want to join us because that will become a necessary evil," he said.
AT&T is believed to be in talks with regional Bell SBC Communications Inc. about a merger that would be the biggest in U.S. corporate history.
